commit_reference_quality.why_it_matters: an abbreviation is a prefix of some commit, not an immutable reference: it resolves only inside a repository someone else controls, and can stop being unique or be rewritten. Each such value is carried as stated by the source and labelled by `commit_reference_kind` in the distribution view, and is never presented as a verified object id. The missing characters are not invented.

decided_by: the dataset builder, from each source's own stated terms and the files in its pinned repository

evidence: the repository root at the pinned commit holds no LICENSE, COPYING or equivalent file
sources.note: the absence of a licence file is not a grant, so the public distribution keeps identifiers, locators and hashes plus an independently written digest, and withholds copied report prose

CC BY-ND 4.0 permits redistributing the licensed work unchanged with attribution and expressly forbids derivatives, so a re-sectioned or rewritten report text is a derivative; that term must stay visible on the record instead of hidden behind license_status: unknown

no licence file is published in the pinned repository, and two of this source's findings additionally state the vulnerable revision as a 38- or 39-character hex string rather than an object id; see commit_reference_quality

what_this_is: A machine-readable record of what each V4 source declares about its own content, and of the data-handling policy this project applies because of it. It is a rights decision about redistribution, not legal advice and not a clearance: no permission was obtained from any source organisation, and none is claimed.
what_this_is_not: It does not establish that any transformed or derived record may be redistributed. Two of the three sources publish no licence at all, which is the absence of a grant rather than a permissive default, and the third declares CC BY-ND 4.0, whose No-Derivatives term is the more restrictive fact that `license_status: unknown` had been hiding in every record.
